title: Trump Says Iran Could Face More Destruction as Options Narrow After Midterms
dek: The president says he may have to "destroy the rest" of Iran, while US forces prepare options and Qatari mediators work on a draft deal.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The Strait of Hormuz, the waterway between Iran and Oman (file photo)

keyPoints: Trump told reporters on Thursday he may have to "destroy the rest" of Iran, Anadolu reported.
Axios reported three options: renewed strikes, negotiation, or sustaining the blockade and sanctions.
US officials told Axios the military is preparing for a possible return to major combat, while Qatari mediators work on a draft agreement.
Vance wrote on X that "The reason we lost is the war," Axios reported.
body:
President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he may have to "destroy the rest" of Iran, while his aides weigh whether to resume bombing, negotiate or keep the current pressure in place, according to Anadolu Agency and Axios.

## What Trump said

Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump said: "I would rather not destroy the rest of the country, if possible, but maybe I'll have to. And you'll know soon enough," Anadolu reported. He also said the decision was whether to go further "and just certify it, by certifying it meaning it will never happen again."

Trump said Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is "doing a very good job," as he dismissed speculation about replacing him, Anadolu reported.

## Three options, per Axios

Axios reported that the president faces three broad paths: strike again, negotiate, or "strangle," a term aides used for keeping the naval blockade and economic sanctions in place while waiting for Iran to yield. Axios wrote that a return to war would be unpopular and could keep gas prices high, and that the strangle option could take months to show progress.

Axios also reported that the US military is finishing preparations for a possible return to major combat operations, including sending more assets to the region, according to American officials. At the same time, Qatari mediators are working to secure US and Iranian support for a draft agreement, regional sources told Axios.

## Politics after the midterms

Trump conceded on Wednesday that the war had hurt Republicans in the midterm elections, Axios reported. Vice President JD Vance wrote on X that "The reason we lost is the war," Axios reported. Trump told reporters Vance's analysis was "largely true" because the war drove gas prices up, while adding that "We had no choice. You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon."

## What we do not know

Neither outlet reported a date for a strike or a signed agreement. Trump has said the war would end "whenever I wanted to," according to Axios.

## Update, Friday midday

The National reported that Iran has sent a nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar, and that it would be discussed only after the US meets Tehran's seven demands, a senior Iranian official told Reuters. A US official said Washington was reviewing it. Araghchi held calls with the foreign ministers of the UAE, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan on Thursday. See the companion story on Iran's seven conditions.
